strengths: Addresses a genuine and timely bottleneck in RL-based mathematical reasoning with a well-motivated problem statement and clear practical value
Rigorous and comprehensive four-stage data curation pipeline featuring sophisticated semantic decontamination, source analysis, and multi-solution consistency checking for answer verification
Strong and consistent empirical results across multiple benchmarks (MATH500, AMC23, Olympiad, Minerva, AIME24/25) with particularly impressive RL-Zero improvements (+6.1 to +30.7%)
Flexible dataset structure supporting multiple training paradigms (SFT, distillation, RL-Zero, reward modeling) increases broad applicability
Broad topical coverage with hierarchical categorization across diverse mathematical domains supporting generalization to unseen problems
Insightful qualitative analysis of RL training dynamics including reasoning length trends and emergent cognitive behaviors (subgoal setting, verification, backtracking)
Public release commitment provides clear value to research community and addresses urgent need for large-scale, challenging, verifiable mathematical data
weaknesses: Limited methodological novelty—curation pipeline primarily combines existing techniques (Toshniwal et al. 2024 decontamination, Gao et al. 2024 difficulty estimation) without introducing fundamentally new methods

Critical missing ablations: no ablation studies isolating contributions of decontamination, difficulty filtering, multiple solutions vs. single solution, or impact of the three R1 solutions individually

Answer verification lacks ground truth validation—relies on R1-generated solutions being correct and uses only consistency checking, not actual correctness verification; no manual spot-checking reported

Experimental design concerns: baseline comparisons may be unfair due to potentially different training procedures and hyperparameters; no statistical significance testing or confidence intervals provided

Incomplete evaluation of decontamination effectiveness—Figure 4 shows raw contamination rates but provides no evidence that decontamination actually improved evaluation integrity or prevented benchmark leakage

Reproducibility limitations: dataset construction depends on proprietary tools (GPT-4o, DeepSeek-R1) that may become unavailable; no code provided; difficulty labels lack reliability analysis (inter-annotator agreement not reported)
Lacks detailed comparative analysis with concurrent work (Big-Math) and missing justification for key design choices (why levels 5+? why these three specific solutions?) without ablations
Limited analysis depth: reasoning length trends and cognitive behaviors provide surface-level insights but lack deeper investigation of what properties make these problems effective for RL training
